correctness.rationale: In the one-positive chamber, exponential conditioning gives sigma(a)=x^{-1} product_j(1+r_j)^(-1) with sum r_j=1. AM-GM yields the sharp ratio bound A/x=1/<a,a_*>=sec(theta), with equality only at the balanced point. Along every unit tangent geodesic through a_*, direct differentiation gives second logarithmic variation (2n-1)/n, and the first variation vanishes, establishing the isotropic Hessian claimed.

originality.rationale: The current global-minimum preprint proves that facet-parallel central sections minimize volume, while the older Dirksen work gives formulas and partial minimum results. Searches did not locate the explicit one-chamber sec(theta) deficit, its coordinate-imbalance form, or the complete isotropic Hessian formula. The claim is appropriately narrow and does not present itself as global stability.

scientific_value.rationale: The theorem supplies an exact quantitative stability inequality and full second variation in a natural chamber, with a very short independent proof that avoids the balancing issue highlighted by the recent global-minimum work. The local Hessian information is useful even though global quantitative stability remains open.

citations.note: Ambrus and Gargyan, Minimal central slices of the regular simplex; current arXiv abstract proves the global facet-parallel minimizer theorem.
Dirksen, Sections of the regular simplex – Volume formulas and estimates; older source for section-volume formulas and partial minimum results.
Myroshnychenko, Tang, Tatarko and Tkocz, Stability of Simplex Slicing; comparison point for stability on the maximal-section side.

findings: The chamber inequality and equality case reduce to a correct one-line AM-GM extremization after the exact exponential-density formula.
The tangent space at a_* is correctly identified by v_1=0 and sum_{j>=2} v_j=0, and the Hessian coefficient is direction-independent.
No source located in the audit states the exact sec(theta) bound or the displayed Hessian.
independent_checks: Re-derived x^{-2}=1+sum r_j^2 and <a,a_*>=x/A, which converts the AM-GM estimate into both displayed deficit formulations.
Differentiated log sigma(a_* cos t+v sin t) along an arbitrary unit tangent direction and recovered (2n-1)/n.
Sampled admissible chamber points in dimensions 3 through 8 and numerically checked nonnegative deficit with equality only at the balanced point.
limitations: The quantitative deficit is confined to one-positive-coordinate chambers and is not global stability.
The exact Hessian is a local statement.
The recent global-minimum preprint creates ordinary residual parallel-work risk, but no directly covering statement was located.
